features.title: Logo lockup

items.question: What size is an X header?
items.answer: 1500×500 px. Design at that size and verify the 600×200 mobile crop separately.

items.question: Where does the avatar overlap?
items.answer: The profile photo covers roughly the left 280 px; keep text and logo out of it.

items.question: Can I put text in the header?
items.answer: Yes, but only two sizes and one block. Text in the avatar zone will be covered.

items.question: How do I keep a campaign header consistent?
items.answer: Reuse the grid, margins and type sizes; only the claim and image change.

body.title: YouTube Thumbnail Generator: 1280×720, Read at 210px
body.highlightedText: A thumbnail is judged at phone size, not at full screen.

body.title: Six decisions before the first export
body.description: CTR is lost at preview size, not at 1280×720.

features.title: Safe margin
features.description: Keep text 6% from every edge; the player chrome covers the bottom.

features.title: Three words
features.description: If the headline needs four, it needs a different idea.

features.title: One face
features.description: A face at 40% of height reads at 210 px; two faces fight.

features.title: Contrast
features.description: Text needs 4.5:1 against the busiest part of the frame.

features.title: Title match
features.description: The thumbnail promise must match the video title.

features.title: Preview test
features.description: Shrink to 210 px; if unreadable, cut a word.

content.title: 1280×720 with margins
content.description: Start at 1280×720, mark 6% margins, leave the bottom band clear of the player bar.

content.title: One subject, one claim
content.description: Pick one face or object at 40% of the height; the rest supports it.

content.title: 210 px check
content.description: Preview at 210 px; if the claim is unreadable, change the words, not the font size.

items.title: The 210 px test
items.description: A thumbnail spends most of its life at phone size. Judge it there: if the claim needs squinting, the design is wrong.

items.title: Title and thumbnail are one promise
items.description: A mismatch between the two is what turns a click into a bounce. Write the claim after the title, not before.

media.alt: Title and thumbnail are one promise

items.title: Faces are chosen at 210 px
items.description: At phone size the expression matters more than the detail. Pick the frame where the face reads first.

items.title: Three words force one idea
items.description: A fourth word usually means two ideas. Cut the idea, not the font size.

items.question: What size should a thumbnail be?
items.answer: 1280×720 px, 16:9. Check it at 210 px to judge real readability.

items.question: How many words fit?
items.answer: Three. Four words force smaller type and lose the preview test.

items.question: Can I use a generated face?
items.answer: Yes, but keep one face at roughly 40% of the height.

items.question: How do I test contrast?
items.answer: Check 4.5:1 against the busiest area, not the average background.

items.question: What does all-in-one mean here?
items.answer: One canvas with several engines and one bill. It does not mean one engine for every task.

items.question: How do I compare engines fairly?
items.answer: Same prompt, same aspect ratio, same export size; judge at 100%.

items.question: Do I need a cost log?
items.answer: Yes. Without one, routing is memory; with one, it is a decision.

items.question: How often should I re-route?
items.answer: Monthly, or when a new engine changes price or quality for your most common task.

body.title: GPT Image Generator: Prompt Adherence Before Style

body.description: Write constraints, check the text and repair the region instead of rerolling. The output is judged against the brief — subject, light, ratio, palette — not against taste.

media.alt: Generated image checked against a written brief

body.title: Six constraints that make a render usable
body.description: Adherence is a checklist, not a mood.

features.title: Subject
features.description: One subject, one action; two subjects fight for the same pixels.

features.title: Light
features.description: Name the key light and its direction.

features.title: Ratio
features.description: Pick 1:1, 4:5 or 16:9 before the render.

features.title: Palette
features.description: Two or three hex values; vibes drift between runs.

features.title: Negatives
features.description: List what must not appear: text, logos, extra hands.

features.title: Text
features.description: If the image must carry words, treat it as a separate job.

content.title: Constraints first
content.description: Subject, light, ratio, palette and a negative list in five lines.

content.title: Three routes, one variable
content.description: Change angle or light between routes; compare at the same size.

content.title: Fix the region
content.description: Repair a hand or a label in the edit layer instead of rerolling the frame.

items.title: The brief is the test
items.description: Adherence means every named constraint is visible: the light direction, the ratio, the palette and the absence of text. If one is missing, the frame is a nice picture, not a delivered brief.

items.title: Text is a separate job
items.description: Generated lettering ships typos. Render a clean plate and set type in the layout tool.

body.title: Two checks before you accept a frame

items.title: Negative list saves a reroll
items.description: Naming what must not appear is cheaper than fixing it after the render.

items.title: Aspect ratio is composition
items.description: Choose the ratio before the render; cropping later moves the subject and breaks the layout.

body.title: From brief to a frame you can keep

steps.title: Repair and export
steps.description: Fix the region, export the sizes the layout needs.

steps.title: Log the rejected pass
steps.description: Keep what failed so the next brief is shorter.

features.title: Concept
features.description: Style range matters more than adherence.

features.title: Product
features.description: Adherence matters more than style.

items.question: Can I use generated images commercially?
items.answer: Depends on your plan; check the license before a paid campaign and keep the record with the asset.

items.question: Why does text come out garbled?
items.answer: Lettering is the hardest detail. Render a clean plate and set type in layout.

items.question: How do I fix one detail?
items.answer: Repair the region in the edit layer instead of rerolling the whole frame.

items.question: What should the brief contain?
items.answer: Subject, light, ratio, palette and a negative list — five lines, no adjectives.
